newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares bounce higher on Lek success.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares bounce higher on Lek success.

text.p: Slovenian shares rebounded 1.99 percent on Wednesday on optimism generated by strident demand for the newly-listed shares of drug maker Lek.
"As expected, demand for Lek was high and pulled the whole market up. The upward trend is expected to last at least until the end of the week," one trader said.
Turnover on the bourse surged to 140 million tolars -- 119.5 million tolars' worth was accounted for by Lek.
Lek today listed 1.7 million shares, taking the total of listed shares to 1.79 million, or 92.7 percent, of the firm's equity. Lek's shares have a nominal value of 6,000 tolars.
* The seven-share SBI index rose 17.71 points to 909.64.
* 10 shares rose and four fell, while 10 were untraded.
* Turnover ballooned to 140 million tolars from 21.1 million.
* Lek's newly-listed shares were the most actively traded, reaching 13,970 tolars on volume of 8,678 shares for total turnover of 119.5 million tolars.
* The previous issue of Lek rose 1.5 percent to 13,900 on volume of 46 shares for total turnover of 0.6 million tolars.
* Brokerage Nika was the leading gainer, surging 6.44 percent to 3,791 on volume of 60 shares for total turnover of 0.2 million tolars.
* Pharmaceutical trader Salus was the leading decliner, falling 3.8 percent to 12,230 on volume of 150 shares for total turnover of 1.8 million tolars.
